title: Drift Calibration in Geometric Eye Tracking Systems
abstract: Geometric eye trackers can provide the spatial accuracy required for gaze-based interaction and multimodal studies, but their measurements remain sensitive to residual session-specific calibration error. Research on correcting this error is difficult to compare because methods are typically evaluated with different devices, target layouts, and error definitions. We present a calibration-focused dataset containing 163 trials from 12 participants, with separate 18-point fitting and 32-point test grids, and use it to evaluate global, local, and composite correction functions under a common spatial-extrapolation protocol. We further introduce a lightweight neural refiner that combines ranked predictions from complementary calibrators. On this controlled dataset, post-vendor correction reduces the mean angular error from $1.53^\circ$ to $1.03^\circ$ with the strongest classical composite and to $0.96^\circ$ with the refiner. In a closed-loop gaze task, lower residual error is associated with higher performance across four online correction conditions. These results provide a reproducible data-quality benchmark for using gaze as a behavioral signal in interactive modeling.

title: Target-Aware State-Adaptive $p$-Dirichlet Graph Neural Regression for Non-Invasive Body-Composition Estimation
abstract: Accurate estimation of body-composition outcomes, including body fat percentage (BFP), bone mineral density (BMD), and appendicular lean mass (ALM), is important for evaluating metabolic, skeletal, and muscular health. Direct assessment using dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA), however, requires specialized equipment and involves ionizing radiation. We propose a target-aware, state-adaptive $p$-Dirichlet energy-flow graph neural regression ($p$SADE-GNR) framework for estimating these outcomes from non-invasive anthropometric measurements. A neural encoder maps participant representations to hidden states that are propagated over an outcome-specific participant-similarity graph by a state-adaptive forward-Euler discretization of the graph $p$-Dirichlet energy flow. Graph distances weight each original or latent coordinate by its normalized absolute training-fold correlation with the outcome. Using clinical data from the Pennington Biomedical Research Center and five-fold cross-validation, the correlation-weighted model using the original standardized measurements achieved the lowest root mean squared error in all nine primary outcome-cohort combinations and outperformed previously reported support vector regression or least-squares support vector regression reference values in eight of nine comparisons. Autoencoder, variational-autoencoder, and Gaussian-mixture variational-autoencoder representations generally did not improve primary-outcome prediction or reduce computational cost. In an exploratory age-prediction analysis including ALM, BMD, and BFP as predictors, the correlation-weighted GMVAE model achieved the lowest mean error in all three cohorts. These results support target-aware, state-adaptive $p$-Dirichlet graph neural regression for non-invasive body-composition estimation.

title: Finding the Way: A Narrative Review of Pathfinding in Game Development, from Dijkstra's Note to Jump Point Search
abstract: Pathfinding is game development's most shipped algorithm: every unit that walks, drives, or flies asks the graph's oldest question—what is the shortest way?—and the field's answers, from Dijkstra's 1959 note through A*'s heuristic guarantee to the games' hierarchical and grid optimizations, constitute the genre's shared infrastructure. This article presents a narrative review of the primary literature of that question, from Dijkstra's 1959 shortest-path algorithm, through Bellman's 1958 routing formulation and Doran and Michie's 1966 graph traverser, Hart, Nilsson, and Raphael's 1968 A*, whose admissible heuristic made search both optimal and informed, Nilsson's 1971 codification, Dechter and Pearl's 1985 characterization of A*'s optimality, Stentz's 1994 D* and Koenig and Likhachev's 2002 D* Lite for replanning, Botea, Müller, and Schaeffer's 2004 hierarchical pathfinding, Bulitko and Lee's 2006 learning real-time search framework, Millington's 2006 Artificial Intelligence for Games, the production codification, and Harabor and Grastien's 2011 jump point search. The synthesis is organized around three themes: the graph's algorithms, in which optimality was defined and achieved; the heuristic's settlement, in which A*'s admissibility became the field's contract and its optimality was characterized; and the games' optimizations, in which hierarchy, replanning, learning, and grid pruning made the search fit the frame. It is concluded that pathfinding's history is one guarantee—optimality at tractable cost—and that the games' contributions, hierarchical and heuristic, are the graph theory's most played applications.

title: A Network Analytic Comparison of Word Associations Generated by Humans and Large Language Models
abstract: Word associations generated by humans and large language models (LLMs) were analyzed using a network science approach to provide insights into their semantic organization. Human data consisted of word associations from the "Small World of Words" project and from native speakers of Singapore English. LLM data were obtained from the "LLM World of Words" project, where three LLMs (Haiku, Llama3, and Mistral) were probed to produce word associations to a large set of cue words. Bipartite network projections onto a subset of cue word nodes enabled a comparison of identical-sized networks that also captured higher-order associative patterns. Human and LLM networks had significantly different global network properties; specifically, human networks appeared to have more well-connected semantic organization than LLM networks, which were more sparsely connected. At the local node-level of the network, the two human networks were more similar to each other than to the LLM networks. Overall, the analyses indicate that latent semantic representations of human word associations are better integrated than those of the LLMs, illustrating how cross-comparisons with LLM-generated data can provide insights into the nature of human semantic representations.

title: Portfolio Risk Bounds without Cross-Asset Return Covariances: Distributional Fields from Language-Model Representations
abstract: Portfolio risk assessment ordinarily relies on reliable estimates of cross-asset return covariances, which are difficult to obtain in short, high-dimensional panels. We show that firm-level distribution-valued characteristics can instead provide one-sided certificates of portfolio risk. Under maintained links from characteristics to systematic exposures and from exposures to returns, multi-firm Wasserstein-2 dispersion yields a sharp upper bound on systematic portfolio variance and a corresponding bound for standardized returns. A weighted pairwise relaxation produces an objective that is convex under a checkable condition and requires marginal volatility scales but no cross-asset return covariances. With zero firm-specific slack, the common-map scale changes the certified variance reduction but not the normalized allocation, which depends only on observed information geometry. In a 52-firm panel from 2018-2022, an allocation constructed from Qwen3-Embedding-8B news representations lies between the 0.69th and 1.33rd in-sample variance percentiles across four prespecified capped portfolio populations; equal risk weighting lies between the 21.1st and 28.6th percentiles. The lower in-sample variance ranking relative to equal risk also appears across the reported frozen language-model representations. The framework therefore distribution-valued firm information into a coherent risk bound and an implementable allocation rule constructed without cross-asset return covariances.

title: Learning in Networks: A Narrative Review of Neural Networks from the Perceptron to Backpropagation and Deep Learning
abstract: Neural networks---learning systems built from simple units connected in layers---survived two winters of disillusion to become deep learning's substrate and artificial intelligence's dominant paradigm. This article presents a narrative review of the field's canonical line: McCulloch and Pitts's 1943 logical neurons, Rosenblatt's 1958 perceptron, Minsky and Papert's 1969 critique, Hopfield's 1982 recurrent networks, the Rumelhart, Hinton, and Williams 1986 backpropagation papers, LeCun's 1989 convolutional networks for zip codes, Glorot and Bengio's 2010 initialization, Hinton and Salakhutdinov's 2006 deep autoencoders, Krizhevsky and colleagues' 2012 AlexNet, Srivastava and colleagues' 2014 dropout, and Ioffe and Szegedy's 2015 batch normalization. The synthesis is organized around three themes: representation, in which network capacity moved from linear separability to universal approximation; learning, in which credit assignment through layered networks was solved by backpropagation and made practical by initialization, dropout, and normalization; and depth, in which the 2012 ImageNet vindication converted four decades of theory into the deep learning era. It is concluded that the neural network's history is AI's clearest case of long-horizon vindication---and that its open problems, interpretability and data appetite, are the field's inheritance.

title: What Discretises a Continuum of Errors Is Not the Code but the Measurement ── Eight Real Parameters Fall to Four Outcomes ── A Distance-3 Code Covers 28 of 262144, That Is 1.07x10^-4 ── [Paper 287]
abstract: The errors that can enter a qubit form a continuum. Why can a code with finitely many correctable errors fix them? This paper asks who does the discretising──the answer is the measurement, not the code. No new mathematical theorem and no new law is claimed. Scope of this paper (scope note): No new mathematical theorem and no new law is claimed──error discretisation, the Pauli basis, stabiliser codes, surface codes, and the threshold theorem are all standard. We do not construct codes──all we count is numbers of parameters and numbers of errors. We do not prove the threshold theorem──the value p_thapprox 10^-2 is quoted as a number only. We do not derive the logical error rate──(p/p_th)^(d+1)/2 is an asymptotic estimate that drops constant factors. The values of Section 5 are orders, not predictions. We do not discuss surface-code implementation──lattice geometry, measurement circuits, and decoders are not treated at all. The count approx d^2 physical qubits is the simplest estimate. We do not treat correlated errors──the count of Section 4 assumes independent single-qubit errors. With correlations, errors leave the weight-1 bracket. We do not read 1.068x10^-4 pessimistically──it is a fraction of all Pauli operators, not a fraction of the errors that actually occur. If real errors concentrate at weight 1, then 28 suffices in practice. This paper does not assert which is the case. On the sibling paper: Paper 281 treats the same quantum error correction and counts that the syndrome tells 8 bits about the error and 0 bits about the state──the root is the same (measurement does not destroy the state) but the question differs. That paper asks what the measurement does not take; this one asks what the measurement makes discrete. Readers are advised to read them side by side. Relation to earlier papers: Paper 163 separated “a good code exists” from “here is a good code”──this paper counts what a constructed code actually covers. Paper 179 showed that “cannot be constructed” has distinct roots──the impossibility of d=4 here likewise has counting as its root. Paper 252 counted four quantities called “information”──this paper separates continuous parameters from discrete outcomes. Paper 269 showed that what a crystal forbids is periodicity──the discretisation here is likewise imposed by a structure. What is added is counting a one-qubit error as 8 real parameters falling to 4 outcomes after measurement, computing that distance 3 covers 28 of 4^9=262144, a fraction of 1.068x10^-4, confirming that 3.24 times in the surface code corresponds to one hundredth, and placing the difference from the classical case at “whether a projection is required”. First, we count the errors on one qubit. E=c_0I+c_1X+c_2Y+c_3Z has 8 real parameters and is a continuum (Section 2). Second, this is the core of the paper. The measurement projects that onto the 4 outcomes I,X,Y,Z──the discretising is done by the measurement, not the code (Section 2). Third, fixing X and Z fixes Y. Since Y=iXZ, only 2 kinds need independent correction (Section 3). Fourth, a code covers only a sliver. Of the 4^9=262144 Pauli operators on 9 qubits, distance 3 fixes 28, a fraction of 1.068x10^-4 (Section 4). Fifth, in the surface code, 3.24 times gives one hundredth. From d=5 to 9, physical qubits 25->81 and logical error rate 10^-3->10^-5 (Section 5). Sixth, the separator is whether a projection is needed. Classical codes need none──because their errors are discrete to begin with (Section 6). The familiar statement that “continuous errors get discretised” is right. But what discretises is the measurement, not the code. A one-qubit error has 8 real parameters and forms a continuum, yet the syndrome measurement projects it onto the 4 outcomes I,X,Y,Z──what remains is a single Pauli error, and undoing it suffices. Since Y=iXZ, only 2 kinds need independent correction. Meanwhile the reach of a code is narrow──of the 262144 Pauli errors on 9 qubits, distance 3 fixes 28, a mere 1.068x10^-4. It works because the assumption that errors are sparse is doing the work. And the price is polynomial──multiplying the physical qubits by 3.24 divides the logical error rate by 100. One thing separates them──whether the errors are discrete to begin with, or a projection is required. A classical code needs no projection. In a quantum code, measuring is a precondition of correcting, and the separate fact that measuring does not destroy the state is what makes it possible. On the making of this work: The ideas and content of this work stem from the author's own considerations. Assistance from an AI (a large language model) was used for structuring, English translation, and checking the algebra. Any remaining errors or misinterpretations are solely the author's. Feedback and corrections are sincerely appreciated. ----- 量子ビットに入る誤りは連続無限にある。それを有限個の符号で訂正できるのは、なぜか。本稿が問うのは、離散化しているのは誰かである──答は、符号ではなく測定である。新しい数学定理も新しい法則も主張しない。 本稿の射程(射程注記):新しい数学定理も新しい法則も主張しない──誤りの離散化、パウリ基底、安定符号、表面符号、閾値定理は、いずれも標準的である。符号を作らない──数えるのはパラメータの個数と、誤りの個数だけである。閾値定理を証明しない──p_thapprox 10^-2 という値は数値として引くのみである。論理誤り率の式を導出しない──(p/p_th)^(d+1)/2 は漸近形の目安であり、定数因子を無視している。第5節の値は「桁」であって予言値ではない。表面符号の実装を論じない──格子の形も、測定回路も、デコーダも一切扱わない。物理量子ビット数 approx d^2 は最も単純な見積りである。相関誤りを扱わない──第4節の数え上げは独立な単一量子ビット誤りを仮定している。相関があれば重み 1 の枠から外れる。1.068x10^-4 を悲観的に読まない──これは全パウリ演算子に対する割合であって、実際に起きる誤りに対する割合ではない。起きやすい誤りが重み 1 に集中していれば実用上は十分である。本稿はどちらが実際かを主張しない。兄弟編について:論文281 は同じ量子誤り訂正を扱い、シンドロームが誤りについて 8 ビット・状態について 0 ビット語ることを数えた──根は同じ(測定が状態を壊さない)だが、問いが違う。あちらは測定が何を取らないか、本稿は測定が何を離散にするかである。読者は両方を並べて読むことを勧める。既刊との関係:論文163 は「良い符号が在る」と「これが良い符号だ」を分けた──本稿は構成された符号が実際に何個の誤りを覆うかを数える。論文179 は「構成できない」に別根があると示した──本稿の d=4 不可も数え上げが根である。論文252 は「情報量」が四つあると数えた──本稿は連続なパラメータと離散な結果を分ける。論文269 は結晶が禁じるのが周期性だと示した──本稿の離散化も構造が課すものである。加えたのは一量子ビットの誤りが実パラメータ 8 つで、測定後に 4 通りになると数えたこと、4^9=262144 に対して距離 3 が覆うのが 28 個・1.068x10^-4 だと計算したこと、表面符号で 3.24 倍が 100 分の一に対応すると確かめたこと、古典との差を「射影が要るかどうか」に置いたことである。 第一に、一量子ビットの誤りを数える。 E=c_0I+c_1X+c_2Y+c_3Z には実パラメータが 8 つあり、連続無限である(第2節)。 第二に、これが本稿の芯である。測定がそれを I,X,Y,Z の 4 通りに射影する──離散にしているのは測定であって、符号ではない(第2節)。 第三に、X と Z を直せば Y も直る。 Y=iXZ だから、独立に直すべきは 2 種類だけである(第3節)。 第四に、符号が直せるのはごく一部である。9 量子ビットのパウリ演算子 4^9=262144 個のうち、距離 3 が直すのは 28 個、割合は 1.068x10^-4(第4節)。 第五に、表面符号では 3.24 倍で 100 分の一である。 d=5->9、物理量子ビット 25->81 で論理誤り率 10^-3->10^-5(第5節)。 第六に、分離子は「射影があるか」である。古典符号には射影が要らない──誤りが最初から離散だからである(第6節)。 量子誤り訂正でよく言われる「連続な誤りが離散化される」は正しい。ただし離散化しているのは符号ではなく、測定である。一量子ビットの誤りには実パラメータが 8 つあり、連続無限であるが、シンドローム測定が I,X,Y,Z の 4 通りに射影する──そのあとに残るのは一つのパウリ誤りであり、打ち消せばよい。 Y=iXZ なので、独立に直すべきは 2 種類である。一方で、符号が覆う範囲は狭い──9 量子ビットのパウリ誤り 262144 通りのうち、距離 3 が直せるのは 28 通り、1.068x10^-4 にすぎない。それでも動くのは誤りが疎だという仮定が効いているからである。そして代償は多項式で済む──物理量子ビットを 3.24 倍にすると、論理誤り率が 100 分の一になる。分けるものは一つ──誤りが最初から離散か、射影を要するか。古典符号に射影は要らない。量子符号では、測ることが訂正の前提であり、測ることが状態を壊さないという別の事実が、それを可能にしている。 作成にあたって:本稿の着想と内容は、著者自身の考察に基づくものです。文章の構成整理や英訳、数式の確認には AI(大規模言語モデル)の助力を得ました。最終的な内容の解釈や誤りがあれば、それらはすべて著者の責に帰します。お気づきの点があれば、ご教示いただければ幸いです。

ビット語ることを数えた──根は同じ(測定が状態を壊さない)だが、問いが違う。あちらは測定が何を取らないか、本稿は測定が何を離散にするかである。読者は両方を並べて読むことを勧める。既刊との関係:論文163 は「良い符号が在る」と「これが良い符号だ」を分けた──本稿は構成された符号が実際に何個の誤りを覆うかを数える。論文179 は「構成できない」に別根があると示した──本稿の d=4 不可も数え上げが根である。論文252 は「情報量」が四つあると数えた──本稿は連続なパラメータと離散な結果を分ける。論文269 は結晶が禁じるのが周期性だと示した──本稿の離散化も構造が課すものである。加えたのは一量子ビットの誤りが実パラメータ 8 つで、測定後に 4 通りになると数えたこと、4^9=262144 に対して距離 3 が覆うのが 28 個・1.068x10^-4 だと計算したこと、表面符号で 3.24 倍が 100 分の一に対応すると確かめたこと、古典との差を「射影が要るかどうか」に置いたことである。 第一に、一量子ビットの誤りを数える。 E=c_0I+c_1X+c_2Y+c_3Z には実パラメータが 8 つあり、連続無限である(第2節)。 第二に、これが本稿の芯である。測定がそれを I,X,Y,Z の 4 通りに射影する──離散にしているのは測定であって、符号ではない(第2節)。 第三に、X と Z を直せば Y も直る。 Y=iXZ だから、独立に直すべきは 2 種類だけである(第3節)。 第四に、符号が直せるのはごく一部である。9 量子ビットのパウリ演算子 4^9=262144 個のうち、距離 3 が直すのは 28 個、割合は 1.068x10^-4(第4節)。 第五に、表面符号では 3.24 倍で 100 分の一である。 d=5->9、物理量子ビット 25->81 で論理誤り率 10^-3->10^-5(第5節)。 第六に、分離子は「射影があるか」である。古典符号には射影が要らない──誤りが最初から離散だからである(第6節)。 量子誤り訂正でよく言われる「連続な誤りが離散化される」は正しい。ただし離散化しているのは符号ではなく、測定である。一量子ビットの誤りには実パラメータが 8 つあり、連続無限であるが、シンドローム測定が I,X,Y,Z の 4 通りに射影する──そのあとに残るのは一つのパウリ誤りであり、打ち消せばよい。 Y=iXZ なので、独立に直すべきは 2 種類である。一方で、符号が覆う範囲は狭い──9 量子ビットのパウリ誤り 262144 通りのうち、距離 3 が直せるのは 28 通り、1.068x10^-4 にすぎない。それでも動くのは誤りが疎だという仮定が効いているからである。そして代償は多項式で済む──物理量子ビットを 3.24 倍にすると、論理誤り率が 100 分の一になる。分けるものは一つ──誤りが最初から離散か、射影を要するか。古典符号に射影は要らない。量子符号では、測ることが訂正の前提であり、測ることが状態を壊さないという別の事実が、それを可能にしている。 title: mT5 Performance in Zero-Shot Cross-Lingual Transfer with Varying Intermediate Task Counts
abstract: Intermediate-task training---fine-tuning a pretrained model on an intermediate task before fine-tuning again on the target task---often improves model performance substantially on language understanding tasks in monolingual English settings. We investigate whether English intermediate-task training is still helpful on non-English target tasks. Using nine intermediate language-understanding tasks, we evaluate intermediate-task transfer in a zero-shot cross-lingual setting on the XTREME benchmark. We see large improvements from intermediate training on the BUCC and Tatoeba sentence retrieval tas Research goal: How does the number of intermediate language-understanding tasks (e.g., 5 vs. 15) affect the zero-shot cross-lingual transfer performance of mT5 on the XTREME-R benchmark when evaluated with BLEU and ROUGE metrics? title: Zero-Override Architecture: Formally Verified Process Flow Integrity for Security Control Enforcement in Payment Systems
abstract: Financial information systems remain vulnerable to process flow integrity breaches when manual overrides circumvent security controls. These breaches exploit the gap between authentication and workflow enforcement. This paper presents the Zero-Override Architecture (ZOA), a framework that structurally prevents the bypassing of verification mechanisms. It analyzes existing architectural weaknesses through formal threat modeling, identifies regulatory compliance gaps, and derives design requirements for tamper-resistant payment processing. The proposed architecture implements a cryptographically attested verification chain in which each processing component must present proof of all preceding control executions before advancing a transaction. The state-transition model, including the exception-handling workflow, is formalized in TLA+ and its completeness, non-bypassability, replay-resistance, and fail-secure properties are verified with the TLC model checker against an explicit adversary capable of component circumvention and attestation replay. Two deliberately weakened baselines, one with a manual override capability and one in which exception approval substitutes for control execution, are refuted by mechanically derived bypass counterexamples. A component ablation identifies which components’ verification the properties depend on. This research contributes to the field by distinguishing process flow integrity from software-level control-flow integrity and establishing it as a discrete security property, providing a reference architecture with formal state-transition specifications, establishing regulatory requirement traceability through explicit control-to-requirement mapping, and creating an evaluation framework applicable across diverse financial information systems.

abstract: This artefact accompanies “Agent-Driven Verification of Memory Safety for liblzma Decoder Components with VST.” It contains the Rocq/VST proof sources for 27 theorems, the verified liblzma source snapshot, generated Clight ASTs, build scripts, and a Dockerfile. title: MMMMM: A Unified Taxonomy for Investigating the Mechanisms of Multilingual MultiModal Misinformation
abstract: Multimodal misinformation on social media is highly prevalent, potent, and harmful, yet difficult to detect and counter, and still poorly understood compared to its text-only counterpart. Research on the properties and deceptive strategies of multimodal misinformation is hindered by a lack of taxonomies grounded in real-world contexts and by the limitations of current multimodal machine learning models, which prevent the automation of annotation and analysis at scale. We address these shortcomings in three steps. First, we collect a large-scale, high-quality dataset of real-world misinformation instances from Twitter/X in seven languages. Second, we develop a novel, comprehensive taxonomy of multimodal misinformation grounded in an in-depth qualitative analysis of the data and prior theoretical work. Finally, we operationalise the taxonomy through an automated multi-step annotation pipeline using a Vision-Language Model (VLM), and perform human-validation. Our novel approach leads to previously undocumented insights about how social media users combine images with text to spread misinformation in the wild, e.g., that AI-generated content is particularly prevalent in technology and science, while vaccination misinformation disproportionately utilises images from news outlets to assert credibility. Our method and findings provide guidance for targeted approaches for detecting multimodal misinformation, and suggest that mitigation efforts should be developed and applied strategically rather than uniformly.

title: Federated Financial Intelligence for Privacy-Preserving Fraud Detection, Credit Risk and Anti-Money-Laundering Analytics
abstract: Abstract: Financial institutions face a shared analytical challenge: fraud, credit losses and laundering patterns can cross organizational boundaries while transaction records and decision rights remain locally governed. This book develops a research framework for federated financial intelligence in which participants coordinate learning under explicit privacy, security and accountability constraints. It distinguishes three tasks with different labels and harms: payment fraud detection, borrower credit assessment and anti money laundering investigation. The proposed evaluation compares federated systems against feasible local baselines, examines selection bias and delayed outcomes, and tests heterogeneous performance across institutions. Threat models cover model update leakage, malicious participants, coordinator failure and cryptographic migration. Five chapters move from institutional foundations to causal reasoning, trustworthy prediction, reproducible operations and applied governance. Ten research themes synthesize relevant works from the supplied bibliography, separating direct financial evidence from transferred methodological approaches. Comparative scenarios in South Asia, Europe, Africa and the Americas illustrate how market structure, connectivity and legal authority shape deployment choices. The central proposition is that a shared model has value only when it improves decision quality under measurable privacy protection, fair treatment, lawful investigation and operational resilience. The book supplies evaluation protocols and decision gates rather than claiming observed gains for a proposed deployment. Keywords federated learning, financial intelligence, fraud detection, credit risk, anti money laundering, privacy, secure aggregation, differential privacy, data governance, anomaly detection, causal inference, calibration, selection bias, model drift, explainability, financial inclusion, auditability, cryptographic lifecycle, investigator workflow, reproducibility

title: Praktische Best Practices für Multithreading: Java-Edition — Konventionen für das Zeitalter der virtuellen Threads (archived 2026-08-30)
abstract: In Java besteht die bewährte Praxis für Multithreading darin, niemals Threads direkt zu erstellen, sondern auf ExecutorService und virtuelle Threads zu setzen. Dieser Artikel fasst die praktischen Prinzipien zusammen: die Wahl zwischen synchronized und ReentrantLock, kooperatives Stoppen über Interrupts, atomare Operationen auf ConcurrentHashMap und den EDT von Swing. Archived version of https://comcomponent.com/de/blog/multithreading-best-practices-java/, as published on 2026-08-30. The live article is maintained and may change after this date. First published 2026-08-02.

title: Security Rests on Three Grounds, and a Quantum Computer Breaks Only One ── RSA at 2048 Bits Is Accelerated by 10^25.3, Yet Multiplying the Key Length by 8 Raises the Quantum Effort Only 512-fold ── What Holds No Information Cannot Be Computed by Any Machine ── [Paper 305]
abstract: The sentence “this cipher is secure” rests on one of three different grounds. This paper asks which of them a quantum computer breaks──the answer is one. No new mathematical theorem and no new law is claimed. Scope of this paper (scope note): No new mathematical theorem and no new law is claimed──the complexity of the number field sieve, Shor’s algorithm, Grover’s algorithm, and the perfect secrecy of the one-time pad are all standard. We do not build cryptography──all we use is one exponent and one mutual information. We do not explain the algorithms──Shor and Grover are quoted by their cost formulas, and we do not enter their workings. We do not discuss implementation security──key management, randomness quality, side channels, and implementation flaws are not treated at all. Most real breaks live there, but this paper treats only the type of ground. We do not discuss the feasibility of quantum computers──neither when nor whether they can be built is treated. Only what would break if they were. We assert no values for the effort──the sieve’s exponent is asymptotic, and 10^25.3 is an order with constants dropped. Only the direction and the order are claimed. We do not treat lattice cryptography──post-quantum schemes also sit on the computational ground, and which problems stay hard under quantum attack is not adjudicated here. Relation to earlier papers: Paper 281 showed that what cannot be copied can still be corrected, and that eavesdropping becomes the number 25%──the third ground here is the physical security shown there. Paper 252 counted four quantities called “information,” needing different things──the second ground here rests on a mutual information that is exactly 0. Paper 112 counted “six distinct roots sharing one rhyme”──“security” here likewise has three distinct roots under one word. Paper 302 treated how existence does not give quantity──computational security likewise sits where “hard” has no settled quantity. What is added is lining up the three grounds by what they depend on, computing the RSA-2048 acceleration as 10^25.3, showing that an eightfold key length raises the quantum effort only 512-fold, and separating symmetric from public key by square root against cube. First, there are three grounds. Computational, information-theoretic, and physical security, and all three depend on different things (Section 2). Second, this is the core of the paper. A quantum computer breaks only the first, and cannot in principle reach the other two (Section 3). Third, the breaking is dramatic. At RSA 2048 bits the ratio of classical to quantum effort is 10^25.3 (Section 4). Fourth, key length cannot answer it. Multiplying the key length by 8 raises the quantum effort only 512-fold (Section 4). Fifth, symmetric keys need only be doubled. Grover gains only a square root, and AES-256 retains an effective 128 bits (Section 5). Sixth, the separator is resting on difficulty against resting on the absence of information (Section 6). “This cipher is secure” rests on one of three different grounds──computational (it is hard), information-theoretic (there is no information), and physical (measuring destroys). A quantum computer breaks only the first──“quantum computers will break cryptography” is one third right. The breaking is indeed dramatic──at RSA 2048 bits the ratio of classical to quantum effort is 10^25.3, and at 4096 bits 10^36.3. And key length cannot answer it──against the classical attack 2538 bits reaches 2^128, while on the quantum side an eightfold key raises the effort only 512-fold. Symmetric keys are another matter──Grover gains only a square root, so AES-256 retains an effective 128 bits. One thing separates them──whether the security rests on difficulty or on the absence of information. Difficulty moves with machines. I(M;C)=0 does not move. Put exactly──a quantum computer breaks the ciphers that rest on difficulty. On the making of this work: The ideas and content of this work stem from the author's own considerations. Assistance from an AI (a large language model) was used for structuring, English translation, and checking the algebra. Any remaining errors or misinterpretations are solely the author's. Feedback and corrections are sincerely appreciated. ----- 「この暗号は安全である」という一文は、三つの別の根拠のどれかに立っている。本稿が問うのは、量子計算機が壊すのはどれかである──答は、一つだけである。新しい数学定理も新しい法則も主張しない。 本稿の射程(射程注記):新しい数学定理も新しい法則も主張しない──数体篩の計算量、ショアのアルゴリズム、グローバーのアルゴリズム、ワンタイムパッドの完全秘匿性は、いずれも標準的である。暗号を作らない──使うのは一つの指数と、一つの相互情報量だけである。アルゴリズムを説明しない──ショアもグローバーも手間の式を引くだけであり、中身には立ち入らない。実装の安全を論じない──鍵管理、乱数の質、サイドチャネル、実装の欠陥は一切扱わない。現実の破られ方の大半はここにあるが、本稿は根拠の型だけを扱う。量子計算機の実現可能性を論じない──いつ作れるかも、作れるかも扱わない。作れたとして何が壊れるかだけを数える。手間の値を主張しない──数体篩の指数は漸近形であり、10^25.3 は定数因子を無視した桁である。比較の向きと桁だけが本稿の主張である。格子暗号を扱わない──耐量子暗号も計算量的安全の側にあるが、どの問題が量子で難しいままかは本稿では判定しない。既刊との関係:論文281 は複製できないのに訂正できることを示し、盗聴が 25% という数になると書いた──本稿の三つ目の根拠はそこで示された物理的安全である。論文252 は「情報量」が四つあり要るものが違うと数えた──本稿の二つ目の根拠は相互情報量が厳密に 0であることに立つ。論文112 は「同じ韻を踏む六つの別根」を数えた──本稿の「安全」も一語の下に三つの別根を持つ。論文302 は存在が定量を教えないことを扱った──本稿の計算量的安全も「難しい」の定量が定まらない側にある。加えたのは三つの根拠を依存先で並べたこと、RSA 2048 bit の加速を 10^25.3 と計算したこと、鍵長を 8 倍にしても量子側が 512 倍にしかならないと示したこと、対称鍵と公開鍵で対処法が違う理由を平方根と三乗で分けたことである。 第一に、根拠は三つある。計算量的安全・情報理論的安全・物理的安全であり、依存先が三つとも違う(第2節)。 第二に、これが本稿の芯である。量子計算機が壊すのは一つ目だけであり、残り二つには原理的に届かない(第3節)。 第三に、壊れ方は劇的である。 RSA 2048 bit で古典と量子の手間の比は 10^25.3 である(第4節)。 第四に、鍵長では対抗できない。鍵長を 8 倍にしても、量子側の手間は 512 倍にしかならない(第4節)。 第五に、対称鍵は倍にすれば済む。グローバーは平方根しか稼がず、AES-256 は実効 128 bitで足りる(第5節)。 第六に、分離子は「難しさに立つか、情報の不在に立つか」である(第6節)。 「この暗号は安全である」は、三つの別の根拠のどれかに立っている──計算量的安全(難しい)、情報理論的安全(情報が無い)、物理的安全(測れば壊れる)である。量子計算機が壊すのは一つ目だけである──「量子計算機が暗号を破る」という一文は、三分の一しか当たっていない。壊れ方は確かに劇的である──RSA 2048 bit で古典と量子の手間の比は 10^25.3、4096 bit では 10^36.3 である。そして鍵長では対抗できない──古典に対しては 2538 bit で 2^128 相当まで行けるのに、量子側は鍵長を 8 倍にしても手間が 512 倍にしかならない。対称鍵は事情が違う──グローバーは平方根しか稼がないので、AES-256 にすれば実効 128 bit で足りる。分けるものは一つ──その安全が、難しさに立っているか、情報の不在に立っているか。難しさは計算機で動く。 I(M;C)=0 は動かない。正確に言えばこうである──量子計算機は、難しさに立つ暗号を破る。 作成にあたって:本稿の着想と内容は、著者自身の考察に基づくものです。文章の構成整理や英訳、数式の確認には AI(大規模言語モデル)の助力を得ました。最終的な内容の解釈や誤りがあれば、それらはすべて著者の責に帰します。お気づきの点があれば、ご教示いただければ幸いです。

We do not build cryptography──all we use is one exponent and one mutual information. We do not explain the algorithms──Shor and Grover are quoted by their cost formulas, and we do not enter their workings. We do not discuss implementation security──key management, randomness quality, side channels, and implementation flaws are not treated at all. Most real breaks live there, but this paper treats only the type of ground. We do not discuss the feasibility of quantum computers──neither when nor whether they can be built is treated. Only what would break if they were. We assert no values for the effort──the sieve’s exponent is asymptotic, and 10^25.3 is an order with constants dropped. Only the direction and the order are claimed. We do not treat lattice cryptography──post-quantum schemes also sit on the computational ground, and which problems stay hard under quantum attack is not adjudicated here. Relation to earlier papers: Paper 281 showed that what cannot be copied can still be corrected, and that eavesdropping becomes the number 25%──the third ground here is the physical security shown there. Paper 252 counted four quantities called “information,” needing different things──the second ground here rests on a mutual information that is exactly 0. Paper 112 counted “six distinct roots sharing one rhyme”──“security” here likewise has three distinct roots under one word. Paper 302 treated how existence does not give quantity──computational security likewise sits where “hard” has no settled quantity. What is added is lining up the three grounds by what they depend on, computing the RSA-2048 acceleration as 10^25.3, showing that an eightfold key length raises the quantum effort only 512-fold, and separating symmetric from public key by square root against cube. First, there are three grounds. Computational, information-theoretic, and physical security, and all three depend on different things (Section 2). Second, this is the core of the paper. A quantum computer breaks only the first, and cannot in principle reach the other two (Section 3). Third, the breaking is dramatic. At RSA 2048 bits the ratio of classical to quantum effort is 10^25.3 (Section 4). Fourth, key length cannot answer it. Multiplying the key length by 8 raises the quantum effort only 512-fold (Section 4). Fifth, symmetric keys need only be doubled. Grover gains only a square root, and AES-256 retains an effective 128 bits (Section 5). Sixth, the separator is resting on difficulty against resting on the absence of information (Section 6). “This cipher is secure” rests on one of three different grounds──computational (it is hard), information-theoretic (there is no information), and physical (measuring destroys). A quantum computer breaks only the first──“quantum computers will break cryptography” is one third right. The breaking is indeed dramatic──at RSA 2048 bits the ratio of classical to quantum effort is 10^25.3, and at 4096 bits 10^36.3. And key length cannot answer it──against the classical attack 2538 bits reaches 2^128, while on the quantum side an eightfold key raises the effort only 512-fold. Symmetric keys are another matter──Grover gains only a square root, so AES-256 retains an effective 128 bits. One thing separates them──whether the security rests on difficulty or on the absence of information. Difficulty moves with machines. I(M;C)=0 does not move. Put exactly──a quantum computer breaks the ciphers that rest on difficulty. On the making of this work: The ideas and content of this work stem from the author's own considerations. Assistance from an AI (a large language model) was used for structuring, English translation, and checking the algebra. Any remaining errors or misinterpretations are solely the author's. Feedback and corrections are sincerely appreciated. ----- 「この暗号は安全である」という一文は、三つの別の根拠のどれかに立っている。本稿が問うのは、量子計算機が壊すのはどれかである──答は、一つだけである。新しい数学定理も新しい法則も主張しない。 本稿の射程(射程注記):新しい数学定理も新しい法則も主張しない──数体篩の計算量、ショアのアルゴリズム、グローバーのアルゴリズム、ワンタイムパッドの完全秘匿性は、いずれも標準的である。暗号を作らない──使うのは一つの指数と、一つの相互情報量だけである。アルゴリズムを説明しない──ショアもグローバーも手間の式を引くだけであり、中身には立ち入らない。実装の安全を論じない──鍵管理、乱数の質、サイドチャネル、実装の欠陥は一切扱わない。現実の破られ方の大半はここにあるが、本稿は根拠の型だけを扱う。量子計算機の実現可能性を論じない──いつ作れるかも、作れるかも扱わない。作れたとして何が壊れるかだけを数える。手間の値を主張しない──数体篩の指数は漸近形であり、10^25.3 は定数因子を無視した桁である。比較の向きと桁だけが本稿の主張である。格子暗号を扱わない──耐量子暗号も計算量的安全の側にあるが、どの問題が量子で難しいままかは本稿では判定しない。既刊との関係:論文281 は複製できないのに訂正できることを示し、盗聴が 25% という数になると書いた──本稿の三つ目の根拠はそこで示された物理的安全である。論文252 は「情報量」が四つあり要るものが違うと数えた──本稿の二つ目の根拠は相互情報量が厳密に 0であることに立つ。論文112 は「同じ韻を踏む六つの別根」を数えた──本稿の「安全」も一語の下に三つの別根を持つ。論文302 は存在が定量を教えないことを扱った──本稿の計算量的安全も「難しい」の定量が定まらない側にある。加えたのは三つの根拠を依存先で並べたこと、RSA 2048 bit の加速を 10^25.3 と計算したこと、鍵長を 8 倍にしても量子側が 512 倍にしかならないと示したこと、対称鍵と公開鍵で対処法が違う理由を平方根と三乗で分けたことである。 第一に、根拠は三つある。計算量的安全・情報理論的安全・物理的安全であり、依存先が三つとも違う(第2節)。 第二に、これが本稿の芯である。量子計算機が壊すのは一つ目だけであり、残り二つには原理的に届かない(第3節)。 第三に、壊れ方は劇的である。 RSA 2048 bit で古典と量子の手間の比は 10^25.3 である(第4節)。 第四に、鍵長では対抗できない。鍵長を 8 倍にしても、量子側の手間は 512 倍にしかならない(第4節)。 第五に、対称鍵は倍にすれば済む。グローバーは平方根しか稼がず、AES-256 は実効 128 bitで足りる(第5節)。 第六に、分離子は「難しさに立つか、情報の不在に立つか」である(第6節)。 「この暗号は安全である」は、三つの別の根拠のどれかに立っている──計算量的安全(難しい)、情報理論的安全(情報が無い)、物理的安全(測れば壊れる)である。量子計算機が壊すのは一つ目だけである──「量子計算機が暗号を破る」という一文は、三分の一しか当たっていない。壊れ方は確かに劇的である──RSA 2048 bit で古典と量子の手間の比は 10^25.3、4096 bit では 10^36.3 である。そして鍵長では対抗できない──古典に対しては 2538 bit で 2^128 相当まで行けるのに、量子側は鍵長を 8 倍にしても手間が 512 倍にしかならない。対称鍵は事情が違う──グローバーは平方根しか稼がないので、AES-256 にすれば実効 128 bit で足りる。分けるものは一つ──その安全が、難しさに立っているか、情報の不在に立っているか。難しさは計算機で動く。 I(M;C)=0 は動かない。正確に言えばこうである──量子計算機は、難しさに立つ暗号を破る。 作成にあたって:本稿の着想と内容は、著者自身の考察に基づくものです。文章の構成整理や英訳、数式の確認には AI(大規模言語モデル)の助力を得ました。最終的な内容の解釈や誤りがあれば、それらはすべて著者の責に帰します。お気づきの点があれば、ご教示いただければ幸いです。

title: The States of the Machine: A Narrative Review of Finite State Machines in Game Development, from Mealy's Circuits to the Game AI's Scripts
abstract: The finite state machine is game AI's oldest architecture: the machine—states, transitions, and the inputs that drive them—formalized in Mealy's 1955 circuits and Moore's 1956 gedanken experiments, proven decidable by Rabin and Scott's 1959, taught by Minsky's 1967 and Hopcroft and Ullman's 1979, extended by Harel's 1987 statecharts, standardized in Booch, Rumbaugh, and Jacobson's 1999 UML, and shipped in the games' scripts of Rabin's 2002 AI Game Programming Wisdom, Schwab's 2004 AI Game Engine Programming, and Buckland's 2005 Programming Game AI by Example. This article presents a narrative review of the primary literature of that architecture, from the automata theory's canon through the statecharts and the UML to the games' production texts, closing with Wagner and colleagues' 2006 Modeling Software with Finite State Machines and Sipser's 2006 Introduction to the Theory of Computation. The synthesis is organized around three themes: the automata's founding, in which the machines' theory—determinism, decidability, and equivalence—was built; the hierarchy's extension, in which statecharts and UML state diagrams scaled the machines to complex systems; and the game settlement, in which the FSM's simplicity—deterministic, inspectable, cheap—made it the game agent's first and most durable architecture. It is concluded that the FSM's game career is simplicity's vindication—and its successors, behavior trees chief among them, its own extensions.

title: ConFormBench: Benchmark Data and Evaluation Artifacts
abstract: ConFormBench is a diagnostic benchmark for evidence-supported record maintenance in conversational form filling. Each item provides a form schema, prior record, visible dialogue history, and current user utterance, and defines the complete supported post-turn record. Version 1.0.0 contains 180 synthetic update turns across crash reporting, grant administration, patient administration, and patent disclosure; the frozen 36/144 development and held-out split; machine-readable schemas; gold records; five held-out baseline architecture runs; additional model-strength runs; evaluator and tool traces; robustness analyses; and pseudonymized materials from a locked 60-item independent-reconstruction audit. The runner, evaluator, baseline systems, analysis scripts, and ConFormBench Studio are available at https://github.com/tveigel/conformbench. The dataset contains no real patient records, crash reports, grant applications, or invention disclosures. Raw annotator submissions and private coordination records are not included.

title: EVESUM: Abstractive Multi‐Document Summarization Focused on Crucial Events
abstract: ABSTRACT Events with their triggers and entity mentions are significant in multi‐document summarization, which provide assistance to the recognition of the vital content of plenty of documents and guarantee the logic of the text. Many existing methods pay attention to leveraging fine‐grained and noun‐centered units like entities to interact with different documents rather than verb‐centered units, where the state changes and salient semantic associations in documents are neglected, causing a lack of logic in summarization. To address these issues, we propose an innovative abstractive multi‐document summarization model focused on events comprised of dynamic triggers and static entities, referred to as Event‐focused Abstractive Multi‐document Summarization (EVESUM), to form high‐quality summaries by explicitly introducing event information from documents. Specifically, we first apply an elaborately designed event‐focused graph attention network to fuse information from events and documents from different encoders, which particularly considers the function of edges in the graph. Additionally, we construct a hierarchical attention mechanism in the decoder to incorporate crucial event messages into summaries, making the generated summaries more succinct, informative, and logical. Experimental results illustrate that compared with state‐of‐the‐art baselines, our model achieves remarkable improvements on the WikiSum and MultiNews datasets.

title: How Prolific Sellers Self-Present: Dissecting the Communication Patterns of 1.6 Million Reverb Listings
abstract: The current paper draws on self-presentation theory and warranting theory to evaluate how the language patterns in an online marketplace reflect seller status (i.e., a prolific seller versus an everyday seller). Using 1.6 million musical instrument listings from Reverb.com in search of content, style, and structural differences in seller product descriptions, the evidence suggested prolific sellers tend to focus more on objective and functional aspects of a product (e.g., its features and specifications) and less on subjective characteristics like tone, relative to everyday sellers. Prolific sellers also communicated in a more narrative-like style, which was driven by an elevated use of personal pronouns, and they used longer descriptions than everyday sellers. Therefore, what prolific sellers focus on tends to be quite technical, but how they communicate this information is typical of a story that is told to potential buyers. Implications for self-presentation theory and warranting theory are discussed.

title: Generalizable Multi-Agent Planning from Signal Temporal Logic Specifications via Diffusion
abstract: Multi-agent systems in the real-world (e.g., drone swarms, autonomous cars, warehouse robots) must satisfy rich, temporal tasks while avoiding collisions. Signal Temporal Logic (STL) elegantly encodes such objectives, but current STL planning methods face critical limitations. State-of-the-art optimization-based approaches can handle arbitrary STL specifications but struggle with scalability, becoming computationally impractical as the number of agents grows. Learning-based methods efficiently handle a large number of agents with rapid planning times but fare poorly when deployment-time objectives differ from those used during training, and do not support planning tasks that require different specifications to be ascribed to different agents (i.e., heterogeneity) or team-level specifications requiring coordination of multiple agents. This fundamental trade-off between generalizability and scalability presents a challenge for realizing multi-agent STL planning algorithms in practice. To overcome this challenge, we introduce a new diffusion method for multi-agent planning with STL specifications. Using a differentiable approximation of STL, we integrate the STL gradient in the denoising process, making our approach generalizable to novel formulas whose predicates are placed anywhere within the goal region covered during training, while achieving the same scalability as existing learning-based methods. Our method supports heterogeneous specifications, and by using diffusion models, naturally enhances plan diversity, thereby significantly reducing safety-related violations (e.g., collisions) among agents. A detailed evaluation study justifies the utility of STL-guided diffusion-based multi-agent planners for constructing generalizable, scalable, and diverse plans. Videos and code are available at https://www.jeappen.com/diff-ma-stl/ and https://github.com/jeappen/diff-ma-stl .

title: News Classification Using Hybrid Natural Language Processing Based Content Modelling with Machine Learning Methods
abstract: With the rapid expansion of digital media, automatic news classification has become essential for managing and filtering the overwhelming volume of online information. Accurate classification enables efficient access to relevant content and supports applications such as personalized recommendations, trend detection, and misinformation control. This study presents a scalable framework for news categorization on a big data platform, improving both effectiveness and efficiency in handling massive datasets. The method integrates Term Frequency–Inverse Document Frequency (TF-IDF) to capture statistical word importance with Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) for deep contextual semantics. Hybrid features are processed in a distributed environment using PySpark for fast and reliable computation. By combining TF-IDF and BERT for hybrid feature representation and processing them with an Extra Trees Classifier (ETC) Machine Learning (ML) model, the framework achieves 90.36% accuracy, demonstrating the effectiveness of integrating statistical, contextual, and ensemble-based learning for robust news classification. Experimental evaluation shows the hybrid model outperforms single-model baselines in both accuracy and robustness. By leveraging TF-IDF, BERT, and PySpark, the framework provides an effective NLP-based solution for real-time news classification and intelligent information management in Big Data.

title: Reproducibility and Generalization Analysis of OCAT Net S for Oral Cancer Image Classification
abstract: Clinical photographs could support earlier referral of suspicious oral lesions, but high internal accuracy does not show whether a model will remain reliable when image source, disease prevalence, or lesion definition changes. This study conducted a secondary experimental analysis of the aggregate measurements reported for OCAT-Net-S by [1]. The analysis examined internal discrimination, component ablation, synthetic perturbation tolerance, computational efficiency, probability calibration, threshold behavior, fold-level dependence, leakage controls, and external transfer. No new patient images or model-training runs were introduced. All new results in this paper are derived from the published tables. OCAT-Net-S achieved an internal AUC-ROC of 0.956, sensitivity of 0.942, and oral-cancer F1-score of 0.942 on 1,238 clinical oral images. Its AUC advantage over TinyViT-5M, the strongest evaluated baseline, was 0.015. The external AUC fell to 0.830 on SMART-OM and 0.840 on the Oral Images Dataset, producing absolute generalization gaps of 0.126 and 0.116. These gaps were 8.40 and 7.73 times larger than the internal advantage over TinyViT-5M. Structural ablations caused a mean AUC loss of 0.046, compared with 0.0128 for training-related ablations. Under the most severe Gaussian-noise condition, OCAT-Net-S retained 96.3% of its clean AUC, compared with 93.8% for TinyViT-5M and 90.3% for ResNet-50. The model used 3.55 million parameters and achieved 0.269 AUC per million parameters, although MobileNetV3-Large remained faster and required fewer operations. Calibration was favorable internally, with a Brier score of 0.0419 and ECE-15 of 0.0174. At an assumed 3% screening prevalence, however, estimated positive predictive value ranged from 0.213 to 0.420 across reported operating points. The findings support the internal technical value of texture-frequency spatial gating and compact local-global feature learning. They also show that distribution shift and prevalence exerted a larger practical effect than the margin separating OCAT-Net-S from its strongest internal comparator. Patient-linked multicenter evaluation, fixed external thresholds, prospective workflow testing, and quantitative lesion localization remain necessary before clinical use.

title: CANON: a chain-anchored normative ontology (reference implementation)
abstract: Reference implementation accompanying the article "Maintaining the normative layer: extending software maintenance standards to the rules that govern AI systems". CANON couples an immutable, human-centred normative core anchored on an append-only governance ledger with a maintainable ontological layer over which six ontology maintenance tasks — mapping, matching and alignment, translation, versioning, integration and debugging — execute as auditable operations. Conflicts within the normative corpus are detected ontologically and classified as resolvable by lexical priority or genuine; genuine conflicts raise a Rule Modification Request adapted from the maintenance process of ISO/IEC/IEEE 14764:2022. Corrections supersede rather than delete. The archive contains the normative core ontology and four embodiment extensions (language-model agent, humanoid robot, in-vehicle AI, edge device), SHACL well-formedness shapes, the conflict detector, the governance ledger and request workflow, the four enactment profiles, a machine-checkable process-coverage report, a seeded conflict corpus with ground truth, and the evaluation harness that regenerates every table and figure reported in the article. The implementation is pure Python and depends only on rdflib, owlrl and pyshacl. It requires no container runtime, Java toolchain or network access, and uses a logical clock so that a run is reproducible bit-for-bit. Reproduce the reported results with python3 -m eval.run_eval.

abstract: notes Based on the indexed array of objects in the stone programming paradigm , stone method from travis raymond-charlie stone on zenodo mapping each word in the dictionary and adding the thesaurus in a heap to make a trie structure control the output in the most likely answer to the prompt, an efficient algorithm is possible A Trie is a data structure that can be used to efficiently manage and search through sequences of tokens, making it suitable for controlling large language models (LLMs) during text generation. By organizing tokens in a tree-like structure, a Trie allows for quick prefix-based searches, which is beneficial for applications like auto-complete and search suggestions. “LLM as a trie” can mean two related ideas: Using a trie to constrain an LLM’s output Thinking of an LLM’s language knowledgeas if it were a trie The first is technically useful; the second is mostly an analogy. A trie, or prefix tree, stores sequences by sharing their prefixes. For example, these phrases: could be represented as: At each point, the trie tells you which next symbols are valid. For an LLM, the symbols are usually tokens, not individual characters. Suppose an application only allows these outputs: After the model generates the token sequence corresponding to "gr", the trie can restrict the next token to one that continues "green". Any token that would produce an invalid phrase is masked before sampling. Conceptually, generation becomes: Pconstrained(t∣x)={PLLM(t∣x),if t is allowed by the trie0,otherwise The remaining probabilities are then renormalized. This is useful for: Autocomplete: only suggest completions ina known vocabulary. Entity linking: generate only valid namesfrom a database. Classification: force the answer to be oneof a fixed set of labels. Structured generation: restrict values tovalid keys, commands, or identifiers. Retrieval systems: efficiently search a largecollection of tokenized phrases. Security-sensitive interfaces: preventgeneration of unsupported commands. A simple character-level implementation might look like this: With an LLM, the same idea is applied to token IDs. During every generation step: Take the tokens generated so far. Find the corresponding node in the trie. Determine the valid next token IDs. Set the logits of all other tokens to negativeinfinity. Sample or select the next token. In practice, there are complications: A word may consist of several subwordtokens. Token boundaries may include spaces orpunctuation. The same text can sometimes have multipletokenizations. A trie may need to store token sequencesrather than strings. If the model generates an invalid token,recovery may require backtracking. Very large tries can consume substantialmemory. An LLM itself is not literally a trie. A trie stores explicit sequences and supports exact prefix lookup. An LLM stores statistical patterns in neural-network weights. It can generalize to phrases it has never seen, while a trie can only follow paths that were inserted into it. A useful comparison is: Trie: “Which continuations are explicitlyallowed?” LLM: “Which continuation is statisticallylikely?” Together: “Which allowed continuation ismost likely?” This combination is often called constrained decoding or grammar-guided generation. A trie works well for finite lists, while grammars, regular expressions, JSON schemas, and parser states are better for more complex structures. The Stone materials describe lookup-oriented structures, indexed variables, parallel string/integer handling, and shifting computation from open-ended evaluation toward precomputed lookup. That maps naturally onto a symbolic language pipeline: dictionary entries become indexed objects, related words become adjacency lists, and the trie represents valid token or word prefixes. A practical architecture would be: Each dictionary object could contain more than a word: The trie would index the token sequence: The thesaurus should not simply substitute every word with every synonym. Instead, it should produce weighted alternatives. For a query word w w, define a candidate score such as: S(c∣w,x)=αPLLM(c∣x)+βRsemantic(c,w)+γF(c)+δC(c,x)−λD(c,w) S(c∣w,x)=αP (c∣x)+βR (c,w)+γF(c)+δC(c,x)−λD(c,w) where: PLLMP is the model’s probability forcandidate cc, RsemanticR measures thesaurus orembedding similarity, F(c)F(c) is frequency or reliability, C(c,x)C(c,x) measures compatibility with theprompt context, D(c,w)D(c,w) penalizes overly distantsubstitutions. A max-heap can retain the best partial paths during search. For example, beam search over the trie can be written as: This produces a trie-guided beam search. The trie removes impossible continuations, while the heap keeps the most promising valid continuations. If the trie contains only approved words or phrases, the output can be guaranteed to belong to that vocabulary. For efficiency, several optimizations matter: Store integer token IDs rather than stringsinside trie edges. Use an array-based or compact double-array trie for cache-friendly lookup. Store synonym links as integer IDs into aseparate array. Keep only the top kk thesaurus relations perword. Cache trie nodes reached by commonprefixes. Batch model scoring for multiple candidatepaths. Use beam search rather than exploring theentire tree. Quantize or precompute static scores wherepossible. Separate immutable dictionary data fromdynamic prompt state. The expected lookup cost is approximately: O(L) O(L) for traversing a prefix of length L L, rather than O(N) O(N) over all N N dictionary entries. Candidate ranking with a heap is approximately: O(Blo⁡K) O(BlogK) per generation step, where B B is the number of candidate expansions and K K is the heap size. The expensive part remains the LLM forward pass, so the main benefit is reducing the number of tokens or paths that must be considered by the model. The strongest design would use three layers: Hard constraint: the trie determines whatoutputs are legal. Semantic expansion: the thesaurus andembeddings determine related alternatives. Probabilistic ranking: the LLM determineswhich legal alternative best fits the prompt. The “State n n” idea described in the related Stone material could also be represented computationally: when several candidates remain close in score, the system does not immediately collapse to one answer. It retains a ranked set of unresolved candidates and continues evaluating them with additional context. zenodo.org However, this system would not automatically produce the “most likely answer” merely because it has a trie. A trie provides structural validity and fast prefix access; it does not provide meaning, truth, or probability. Those must come from language-model scores, retrieval evidence, semantic similarity, or a separately trained ranking function. A useful name for the combined method would be: Indexed Thesaurus Trie with Heap-Guided Constrained Decoding or, more compactly: IT-HCD: Indexed Trie Heap-Constrained Decoding That is a feasible algorithmic direction, especially for domain-specific assistants, command systems, autocomplete, controlled vocabularies, and symbolic reasoning. The key benchmark would compare it against ordinary beam search on: latency, memory usage, tokens evaluated, top-1 and top-kk accuracy, invalid-output rate, semantic relevance, and quality when the correct answer is notexplicitly present in the dictionary To implement the logic described—combining an indexed array of dictionary objects (for the base structure), a heap-based thesaurus (for semantic expansion), and a trie (for output control)—you can create a pipeline that filters the LLM's probability distribution through a dynamic "allow-list." Here is an efficient algorithmic approach to achieve this. ### 1. The Data Structures * **The Dictionary Trie:** Instead of a standard trie, use a **Token-Trie**. Each node represents a token ID. This trie maps every word in the dictionary. If the model starts generating a phrase, the trie identifies the only valid token IDs that could follow. * **The Thesaurus Heap:** A heap is typically used for priority. In this context, you can use a **Max-Heap of semantic associations**. For any given word in the dictionary, the heap stores related words (synonyms/hypernyms) sorted by "strength" or "relevance." * **The Indexed Array:** This serves as the O(1) lookup table to map word strings to their corresponding Trie nodes and Heap priorities. ### 2. The Algorithm: Semantic Constraint Decoding The goal is to ensure the LLM chooses the most likely answer that is *both* linguistically valid (via the dictionary) and semantically enriched (via the thesaurus). **Step-by-Step Execution:** 1. **Prompt Processing:** The LLM generates a probability distribution (logits) for the next token $T_{next}$. 2. **Trie Filtering (Hard Constraint):** * Check the current state of the generated sequence in the **Trie**. * Identify the set of "Dictionary-Valid" tokens $V_{dict}$. * Mask all tokens in the LLM output that are not in $V_{dict}$. 3. **Thesaurus Expansion (Soft Constraint/Weighting):** * Look up the current token in the **Indexed Array**. * Extract the **Thesaurus Heap** for that token. * Pop the top $N$ most relevant syno

title: Compatibility Restores Spin Alignment for Three Qubits
abstract: We study a spectral majorization problem for lifted quantum marginals. For every three-qubit state, every single-qubit replacement state, arbitrary nonnegative weights on all eight supports, and compatible marginals arising from one global state, we prove that the weighted marginal sum is majorized by the perfectly aligned construction. This yields simultaneous bounds for all Schur-concave spectral entropies, together with a trace-norm robustness statement and a quantitative incompatibility witness. The proof isolates compatibility to the overlapping-pair sector and establishes unconditional bounds for the remaining extreme-ray families. We also prove several strict four-qubit slices, including endpoint and complement-symmetric prefixes, an equal-singleton rank-two ray, and a symmetric one-excitation Dicke family. The unrestricted noncommuting four-qubit middle-rank problem remains open. The deposited source package contains the exact certificates and reproducibility scripts.

title: Spatial Matryoshka Training for Multi-Granularity Visual Document Retrieval
abstract: Multi-modal late-interaction retrievers achieve strong retrieval on visually rich documents by representing each page as per patch embeddings and matching at the token level. However, this approach incurs high storage costs. Existing compression methods typically fix a single compression level at indexing time, limiting flexibility. We present ColSNAP (Spatial Nested Average Pooling)1, a training method that generates a nested hierarchy of compression levels directly from a backbone's patch grid. By spatially pooling patch embeddings into pro- gressively coarser tiers and training all tiers simultaneously, a single model learns to support retrieval at multiple compression levels without architectural changes. Crucially, a single encoding pass yields every tier, enabling the accuracy-storage trade-off to be configured at indexing time to match avail- able storage budgets, rather than being fixed during training. We demonstrate that models trained using ColSNAP maintain near full-resolution retrieval performance under substantial compression and that ColSNAP transfers effectively across multiple late-interaction backbones, and achieves most of its improvements via a lightweight adaptation stage applied to a pre-trained retriever.

title: On the Number of Observation Nodes in Recurrent Neural Networks with Linear Threshold and ReLU Functions
abstract: This paper investigates how node update rules and admissible state domains affect the minimum number of observation nodes required for global finite-horizon observability in recurrent neural networks with linear-threshold and ReLU update functions. Over a common binary state domain, we construct a class of $K$-linear-threshold ($K$-LT) networks whose initial states can be uniquely reconstructed from the finite output trajectory of a single observation node. We further establish a dynamical equivalence between binary-valued $K$-ReLU networks and $K$-AND Boolean networks, which transfers existing class-level observation-node bounds to binary-valued $K$-ReLU networks. For nonnegative-valued ReLU networks, the observability problem reduces to the classical linear-system setting whenever the relevant pre-activations remain nonnegative. For general real-valued ReLU networks, we prove that global finite-horizon observability requires at least $n/2$ observation nodes when no restriction is imposed on the number of state variables involved in each node update. This lower bound is tight when $n=2K$, for which we construct a $K$-ReLU network observable from exactly $K$ nodes. These results show that both update rules and state domains fundamentally affect extremal observation requirements: temporal evolution can concentrate finite-state information into a single measured trajectory, whereas activation-induced rank loss creates an intrinsic sensor lower bound in continuous-state ReLU networks.

title: SpatialTrust: A Benchmark for Environmental Risk Recognition in Secure Authentication
abstract: Visual environmental risk recognition plays an important role in secure authentication, where a user's surroundings may reveal sensitive information or introduce potential security risks. However, existing evaluations of multimodal large language models (MLLMs) rarely examine whether models can reliably recognize, localize, and explain such risks in spatially grounded authentication scenarios. We present SpatialTrust, a question-answering benchmark for evaluating environmental risk recognition in secure authentication. SpatialTrust assesses five complementary abilities: sensitive factor detection, direct factor identification, indirect factor identification, direct factor explanation, and indirect factor explanation. We evaluate both proprietary and open-source MLLMs and find that current models show limited performance, especially in understanding and explaining indirect risks, indicating that spatial risk awareness remains a challenging capability for MLLMs. In addition, we introduce SpatialTrustGuard, a structured QA-and-audit pipeline that improves Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B-Instruct from 36.78% to 41.12% overall. Our findings highlight the need for dedicated benchmarks and structured inference methods to improve the trustworthiness of MLLMs in secure authentication.

title: How to Build Strategic Differentiation with Customized GenAI
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) systems have been heralded as transformative technologies. While early adopters may gain short-term advantages, competitive advantage from adoption alone is often short-lived as similar models become widely available. To address this challenge, companies are developing customized and agentic GenAI systems, fine-tuned and trained with proprietary data, and tailored to specific industries and use cases. Drawing on cross-industry data and our interviews with industry experts, we identify three customization approaches in GenAI development— and examine the opportunities and challenges companies face in applying them.

title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND WHOLE-SLIDE IMAGING IN CYTOPATHOLOGY: TECHNICAL CONSIDERATIONS, EVIDENCE, AND WORKFLOW INTEGRATION
abstract: Objective: To review the technical challenges, published evidence, validation considerations, and practical workflow integration of Whole-Slide Imaging (WSI) and Artificial Intelligence (AI) in gynecologic and non-gynecologic cytopathology. Methods: A narrative review was undertaken using peer-reviewed literature on digital cytopathology, WSI, AI-assisted cytology, validation studies, and standardized reporting systems. Emphasis was placed on reported study populations, diagnostic performance, validation approaches, workflow effects, and limitations of current models. Results: While digital histopathology has achieved widespread clinical adoption, digital cytopathology faces distinct physical constraints, including three-dimensional cellular overlapping, variable depth-of-field, liquid-based preparation variations, and massive digital file sizes. Recent developments in multi-layer z-stacking, fast volume scanning, and deep learning models have significantly advanced automated cell detection and classification across standardized reporting schemes (including Bethesda, Paris, Milan, Sydney, and TIS). However, routine clinical implementation remains dependent on specimen and scanner standardization, laboratory-specific validation, interoperability, infrastructure, regulatory requirements, and continued cytopathologist oversight.

title: Scaling Intermediate-Task Training Data for Zero-Shot Cross-Lingual Accuracy in mT5
abstract: Intermediate-task training---fine-tuning a pretrained model on an intermediate task before fine-tuning again on the target task---often improves model performance substantially on language understanding tasks in monolingual English settings. We investigate whether English intermediate-task training is still helpful on non-English target tasks. Using nine intermediate language-understanding tasks, we evaluate intermediate-task transfer in a zero-shot cross-lingual setting on the XTREME benchmark. We see large improvements from intermediate training on the BUCC and Tatoeba sentence retrieval tas Research goal: What is the impact of scaling the intermediate-task training dataset size in English on the zero-shot cross-lingual accuracy of mT5 on XTREME-R while maintaining constant inference efficiency? title: Hybrid method for identification of speech signals acquired by a distributed fiber optic sensor
abstract: Distributed Acoustic Sensing (DAS) has emerged as a promising technology for monitoring and information-security applications due to its ability to provide continuous distributed sensing over long distances using standard optical fibers. However, speech signals acquired by DAS systems are characterized by low signal-to-noise ratios, spectral instability, environmental interference, and significant distortions, which complicate automatic speech recognition and speaker identification. This paper presents a hybrid approach for the processing and identification of speech signals acquired by a distributed fiber-optic acoustic sensor. The proposed framework combines Probability Difference-Based Temporal Fusion (PDTF), Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT), Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCC), Common Spatial Patterns (CSP), and Support Vector Machine (SVM) classification. A review of contemporary methods for DAS-based speech processing is conducted, and the role of time-frequency analysis, perceptually motivated feature extraction, temporal fusion, and machine-learning techniques is discussed. The proposed framework integrates temporal, spectral, perceptual, and spatial information within a unified processing pipeline designed to improve the robustness of speaker identification under noisy operating conditions. The analysis indicates that hybrid signal-processing architectures provide significant potential for DAS-based speech recognition by combining the advantages of classical signal-processing methods and machine-learning algorithms. The presented approach may be applied in information-security systems for covert monitoring, personnel authentication, intruder detection, perimeter protection, and critical-infrastructure security. Future research directions include adaptive noise-suppression techniques, self-supervised learning methods, multimodal data fusion, and the development of specialized benchmark datasets for DAS-based speech-recognition systems.

title: The Policy Deficit in AI x Social-Emotional Learning Research
abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly integrated into social-emotional learning (SEL) initiatives, the need for evidence-based policy has become paramount. We systematically reviewed 65 peer-reviewed papers that examine the intersection of AI and SEL to investigate how these studies articulate policy implications. Our analysis revealed a substantial "policy deficit" in the current AI x SEL literature: nearly three-quarters of the studies did not mention policy implications at all. Using the "WH-question" framework (Who, What, Why, When/Where, and How), we map the policy implications narratives present in the literature and show that they often lack the specificity and actor-oriented guidance required for effective evidence-informed policymaking. We find a significant association between publication venue and policy engagement, suggesting that current academic incentive structures may prioritize technical innovation and pedagogical feasibility over explicit engagement with governance and regulation. This study identifies a "techno-solutionist" trap, where technical potential is foregrounded while the institutional conditions for responsible implementation remain under-specified. We conclude by proposing a shift from "implication-as-afterthought" to "implication-as-methodology" and offer a set of actionable guidelines for researchers, editors, reviewers, and policymakers to bridge the gap between AI innovation and educational governance. Rather than presenting policy as a generic ethical horizon, we argue that AI-SEL studies should systematically specify Who should act, What actions are recommended, Why these actions are needed, When and Where they apply, and How strongly they are framed, thereby strengthening the translation of AI x SEL innovation into educational policy and practice.

title: Wasserstein-Barycentric Interaction Fields for Spatial Factor Models: Evidence from Language-Model Representations
abstract: Spatial return models take the interaction matrix as given and leave feedback uninterpreted. We construct a bandwidth-free field from firms' language-model article embedding distributions using target-anchored Wasserstein barycentric reconstruction. A quadratic exposure-adjustment problem maps feedback into a peer-misalignment penalty ratio. For 52 firms, the field, frozen from 2018-2022 news, yields a 2023-2026 penalty ratio of 3.46 (95% interval [2.89, 4.17]) and higher conditional quasi-likelihood than equal-weighted peer support or RBF weighting of the same distances. Joint penalty ratios for the barycentric and news co-mention fields are 2.33 and 0.86 with boundary calibrated tests which reject both exclusions.

title: GeoAgent: Evaluating VLM Geolocalization Through Embodied Navigation
abstract: Modern Vision-Language Models (VLMs) perform well above the human baseline in image geolocalization, a task critically important in disaster response, OSINT verification, and location privacy. However, most efforts to study AI behavior on the task remain limited to static image-based retrieval, classification, and predictions. We argue that faithful recreation of the task should involve embodied navigation, where a multimodal agent autonomously explores its surroundings to gather observations before submitting a prediction. To this end, we introduce \textbf{GeoAgent}, an agentic environment-based benchmark that requires agents to navigate Street View environments to refine their geolocalization through sequential reasoning. Our analysis shows that modern VLMs struggle to discern regional patterns while succeeding at country- and continent-level predictions. When compared to static image-based baselines, agentic navigation significantly improves accuracy across established metrics. We also note severe bias in a developed/developing region context across frontier model architectures and poor self-improvement capabilities given incorrect priors. Overall, our work establishes the challenges of embodied navigation and geospatial reasoning. We publicly release our code and the GeoAgent environment: https://geoagent-benchmark.github.io

title: VAYAS: An Age-Stratified Zero-Shot Audit of Hindi Speech Recognition
abstract: We present a zero-shot audit of four automatic speech recognition (ASR) systems for Hindi, examining whether word- and character-error rates differ by speaker age under a matched-cohort design. Common Voice Hindi, the most widely used open Hindi ASR benchmark, turns out to have almost no confirmed elderly speakers once its self-reported age field is actually counted (2 in their 60s, 0 older, out of 369 speakers). We instead use IndicVoices-R Hindi, a public spontaneous-speech corpus with genuine elderly (age 60+) representation, comparing 50 elderly speakers against a duration-matched, same-corpus control cohort across four systems: OpenAI Whisper large-v3, Meta MMS-1B, and two India-specialized models, AI4Bharat's IndicConformer and IndicWhisper. IndicConformer achieves the lowest error rates by a wide margin, though we flag a serious, unresolved training-data contamination risk on this result. IndicWhisper is the weakest performer, partly explained by a decoder repetition-loop failure mode. Age-cohort effect sizes are small across all four systems (Cohen's d < 0.2 in every case); one nominally significant elderly disadvantage (IndicWhisper) does not survive correction for multiple comparisons and is below this sample's minimum detectable effect size, so we report it as suggestive, not confirmed. We release the full zero-shot audit pipeline, matched-cohort sampling code, and per-clip results.

title: A Tight Ceiling for Coset-Split Magic-Cat-State Decompositions: dim(A) ≤ m/2 is Optimal for Every Z4-Quadratic Affine Subspace of E_m, for Every Even m
abstract: 10.5281/zenodo.22167895 ("Magic Cat States VII") proves χ(catm) ≤ 2m/2−1 for every even m via an explicit "domino" coset-split construction: pair up all m bit positions into m/2 disjoint cyclically-adjacent pairs, split the even-weight code Em into 2m/2−1 cosets of the resulting subspace, and verify the cubic cat-state phase restricts to a genuine Z4-quadratic (stabilizer) phase on every coset. This deposit proves that construction is not merely a good one — it sits at a hard ceiling that applies to every coset-split subspace of Em, of any shape, disjoint-support or not. Theorem. For every even m, every Z4-quadratic affine subspace A of the even-weight code Em satisfies dim(A) ≤ m/2. Proof (elementary). For x,y in Em, the weight identity w(x⊕y) = w(x)+w(y)−2|x&y| gives, with g(v) := popcount(v)/2 mod 4, the unconditional identity B(x,y) := g(x⊕y)−g(x)−g(y) ≡ −|x&y| (mod 4) on all of Em. "A is Z4-quadratic" means B restricted to A is Z4-bilinear. Using the exact identity |x&(y⊕z)| = |x&y|+|x&z|−2|x&y&z|, bilinearity of B on A is equivalent to |x&y&z| being even for every x,y,z in A. Specializing z=y (a valid triple since x,y ∈ A) gives |x&y| even for all x,y ∈ A — i.e. A is totally self-orthogonal under the standard (nondegenerate) F2 dot product, so A ⊆ A⊥, forcing dim(A) ≤ dim(A⊥) = m − dim(A), i.e. dim(A) ≤ m/2. Dominoes attain dim(A) = m/2 exactly — the ceiling is not just unmet by search, it is provably tight. Verification. Every step checked computationally before being trusted: the identity above holds on 1,000 random pairs each at m=4 through 32; an independently-implemented O(dim³) equivalence test (triple-intersection parity) agrees with the original finite-difference test on all ~1,500 random subspaces checked at m=4 through 12, with zero exceptions; an explicit greedy search built specifically to try to exceed the ceiling (m=6 through 16, 40 restarts each, prefiltered by the necessary conditions this proof derives) never got past dim = m/2 in any restart; dominoes attain the ceiling exactly at every m checked, m=4 through 64. Consequence. This closes the coset-split family as a whole: no subspace shape, disjoint-support or otherwise, can produce fewer than 2m/2−1 cosets while keeping the phase condition that makes each piece a genuine stabilizer state. The family's exponent log₂(χ)/(m−2) = 1/2 exactly, for every m, is now a proven fact about the entire construction class, not an empirical pattern across a handful of measured m. It does not approach the Qassim–Pashayan–Gosset target exponent log₂(3)/4 ≈ 0.396241 at any m — this result establishes that no refinement within the coset-split family ever will, closing that avenue rather than merely reporting it unexplored. Files: CEILING_PROOF.md (full derivation and verification writeup), ceiling_proof.py (the verification script — identity checks, the equivalence test, the counterexample search, dominoes-attain-the-ceiling check), ceiling_proof.log (its output).
