title: Federated Learning for Anomaly Detection in Satellite Constellations Using an Attention-Based LSTM-Autoencoder
abstract: As satellites become more complex and satellite constellations grow, there is a need for privacy-preserving and autonomous anomaly detection systems that can function under harsh communication and computational limitations. In this paper, federated learning is proposed for anomaly detection in satellite telemetry data, using an attention based LSTM autoencoder. To overcome these key privacy and bandwidth constraints in space-based systems, our system allows multiple satellites to jointly train a shared anomaly detection model without sharing any raw telemetry data. We propose an architecture that integrates temporal attention with LSTM autoencoders, allowing for the capture of temporal events over long horizons and subtle anomalous event patterns in multivariate telemetry streams. Our framework is evaluated using a synthetic satellite telemetry dataset, under centralized, local only and federated learning approaches in different configurations. Our primary contribution is the architectural integration of federated learning with attention-based LSTM autoencoders, rather than achieving state-of-the-art anomaly discrimination. Our federated attention-LSTM autoencoder can obtain a validation loss of 0.7221 and anomaly detection rate of 5.00% with total communication overhead of 1.01 MB in five satellite clients. The attention mechanism demonstrates greater stability in reconstruction error with a reduction of 95.3% in the standard deviation compared to standard LSTM autoencoders. The AUC score of 0.5105 indicates that the current model performs near-random in terms of anomaly discrimination; we therefore focus on the framework's architectural and communication advantages. Our results confirm that FL is a viable, privacy-respecting, communication-efficient paradigm for onboard satellite anomaly detection in a resource-constrained constellation environment, while honestly acknowledging performance limitations and positioning this work as a foundational architectural framework.

evidence.title: Federated Learning for Anomaly Detection in Satellite Constellations Using an Attention-Based LSTM-Autoencoder
evidence.abstract: As satellites become more complex and satellite constellations grow, there is a need for privacy-preserving and autonomous anomaly detection systems that can function under harsh communication and computational limitations. In this paper, federated learning is proposed for anomaly detection in satellite telemetry data, using an attention based LSTM autoencoder. To overcome these key privacy and bandwidth constraints in space-based systems, our system allows multiple satellites to jointly train a shared anomaly detection model without sharing any raw telemetry data. We propose an architecture that integrates temporal attention with LSTM autoencoders, allowing for the capture of temporal events over long horizons and subtle anomalous event patterns in multivariate telemetry streams. Our framework is evaluated using a synthetic satellite telemetry dataset, under centralized, local only and federated learning approaches in different configurations. Our primary contribution is the architectural integration of federated learning with attention-based LSTM autoencoders, rather than achieving state-of-the-art anomaly discrimination. Our federated attention-LSTM autoencoder can obtain a validation loss of 0.7221 and anomaly detection rate of 5.00% with total communication overhead of 1.01 MB in five satellite clients. The attention mechanism demonstrates greater stability in reconstruction error with a reduction of 95.3% in the standard deviation compared to standard LSTM autoencoders. The AUC score of 0.5105 indicates that the current model performs near-random in terms of anomaly discrimination; we therefore focus on the framework's architectural and communication advantages. Our results confirm that FL is a viable, privacy-respecting, communication-efficient paradigm for onboard satellite anomaly detection in a resource-constrained constellation environment, while honestly acknowledging performance limitations and positioning this work as a foundational architectural framework.

title: Neural ODE enhanced linear mixed effect models for estimating complex association patterns of time-varying covariates with the marker trajectory
abstract: Longitudinal cohort studies produce repeated data that enable the assessment of time-varying association patterns between exposures and health outcomes. Classical linear mixed-effects models (LMMs) can accommodate a large variety of association patterns while accounting for the irregularly spaced, partially observed measurement. But they require the analyst to pre-specify the functional form linking the exposure history to the outcome. We propose the Neural ODE-LMM, which embeds a Neural Ordinary Differential Equation (Neural ODE) within the linear mixed-effects framework: a learned vector field encodes covariate trajectories into a continuous-time latent state that drives both the fixed- and random-effect design, while preserving the standard LMM observation model. This retains classical likelihood-based inference while learning complex, potentially cumulative, covariate effects flexibly. All parameters are estimated by maximising a penalised marginal likelihood. To quantify covariate effects, we introduce contrasts of counterfactual predictions that compare the expected outcome under alternative covariate trajectories with variance estimated via the delta method. In simulations, the model recovers both instantaneous and cumulative-burden effects without prior specification of the functional form. Applied to the Trois-Cités (3C) cohort, a population-based study of 7{,}324 participants, the method reveals trajectory-dependent associations of BMI and fasting glucose with cognitive decline.

title: Probability-based Estimates of the Uncalculated N^5LO QCD Contribution to the Hadronic W-Boson Decay Width
abstract: The perturbative QCD corrections to the hadronic decay width of the W boson are currently known up to next-to-next-to-next-to-next-to-leading order (N^4LO), whereas the exact N^5LO correction remains unavailable owing to its formidable computational complexity. In this work, we estimate the N^5LO contributions by adopting Bayesian analysis (BA). Before performing the estimation, the Principle of Maximum Conformality (PMC) is employed to improve the precision of the initial scale-dependent perturbative series. Through recursive application of the renormalization group equation, non-conformal terms are absorbed into the strong running coupling, yielding a scheme-independent, scale-invariant perturbative series with improved convergence. The PMC procedure determines an effective coupling α_s(Q_*), with the PMC scale fixed as Q_* = 100.102~GeV at next-to-next-to-leading logarithmic accuracy. Based on the improved and more precise series, the 95.5% BA credible interval yields an uncertainty of Δδ_QCD|_{PMC, BA}^{N^5LO} = pm 1.0times 10^{-5}. The resulting hadronic branching ratio is B(Wto hadrons)|_PMC = (65.84pm 1.54)%, which is consistent with experimental data within reasonable errors.

title: Task-Relevant Feature-Dynamics Fidelity Enables Zero-Shot Sim-to-Real Transfer for Robotic Ultrasound Scanning
abstract: Robotic ultrasound policies operating directly on B-mode images require extensive interaction data, whereas real-robot data collection is costly and safety-constrained. Simulation provides a scalable alternative, but zero-shot transfer depends not only on single-frame realism but also on whether simulated observations reproduce task-relevant feature changes induced by probe motion. We term this cross-domain consistency task-relevant feature-dynamics fidelity (TR-FDF). Under local regularity assumptions, our contraction analysis shows that greater sensitivity of TR-FDF mismatch to probe motion reduces the effective closed-loop contraction margin, whereas motion-independent errors primarily enlarge the residual error bound. Guided by this analysis, we develop a TR-FDF-oriented ultrasound simulator that combines a shared structural intermediate domain, trajectory-level fixed noise, and few-step conditional flow generation. In phantom experiments, a policy trained exclusively in simulation succeeded in 390 of 400 zero-shot deployments across four target planes. The simulator achieved an FID of 29.66 and generated observations at 67.1 Hz. Controlled interventions, ablations, and baseline comparisons showed that TR-FDF sensitivity complements single-frame realism in predicting zero-shot transfer performance.

title: SIC-Agents: Benchmarking and Building an Adaptive Simulator for Pediatric Serious Illness Communication Training
abstract: Pediatric serious illness communication (SIC) is critically important, yet scalable communication training for clinicians remains limited. Compared with other dialogue simulation settings, pediatric SIC poses additional challenges, including multi-party interactions, response to parental distress and strong dependence on feedback dynamics. Existing LLM-based simulators optimize generic dialogue quality rather than curriculum-contingent behavior required for effective SIC training. In collaboration with educators and pediatric clinicians, we introduce the first benchmark suite and simulation framework tailored to pediatric SIC training. Our benchmarks, PitfallBench and DialogueBench, evaluate simulators both at the turn-level and across full dialogues. We further propose SIC-Agents, a self-improving framework that generates a clinician-editable skill document to guide simulator behavior. Our experiments show that SIC-Agents outperforms static expert prompting. To support future research, we release our benchmarks for parent simulation in pediatric SIC at https://github.com/Beikewzh/sic-benchmarks

title: Best practices לריבוי threads בפועל: Java — המוסכמות בעידן ה-virtual threads (archived 2026-08-30)
abstract: ב-Java הנוהג המבוסס ב-multithreading הוא לא ליצור threads ישירות אלא לבנות על ExecutorService ועל virtual threads. המאמר מציג את העקרונות המעשיים: בחירה בין synchronized ל-ReentrantLock, עצירה שיתופית באמצעות interruption, פעולות אטומיות ב-ConcurrentHashMap, ו-EDT של Swing. Archived version of https://comcomponent.com/he/blog/multithreading-best-practices-java/, as published on 2026-08-30. The live article is maintained and may change after this date. First published 2026-08-02.

title: LiTRA: Lightweight TLS Record-layer AEAD benchmark dataset
abstract: LiTRA records the cost of running NIST Lightweight Cryptography AEAD algorithms as TLS 1.3 record-layer ciphers on embedded hardware. Five NIST LWC finalists are measured alongside the two standard TLS 1.3 baselines and an integrity-only control across twelve payload sizes, seven batch sizes, and five CPU clocks on a pair of ESP32-P4 boards communicating over Ethernet. Every row summarizes one batch of TLS records and carries 29 fields, spanning latency, throughput, cycle counts, per-byte cost, heap and stack consumption, and the static memory footprint of each cipher. The two boards are synchronized with IEEE 1588 Precision Time Protocol, so the client and server files are paired observations of the same traffic recorded from opposite ends of the link. The deposit holds five archives, one per CPU clock, each containing a client and a server CSV file. Field names, units, and provenance are documented in column_dictionary.csv. Measurement setup, experimental design, archive composition, and coverage notes are given in README.md, which should be read before use. Measurements were taken with ESP-IDF v5.5.2 and wolfSSL 5.7.2 extended with a cryptographic abstraction layer that exposes lightweight AEAD algorithms through the TLS 1.3 record layer.

title: A parallel corpus of Akkadian transliterations and English translations
abstract: AkkadNMT-75K: Akkadian–English Parallel Corpus AkkadNMT-75K is an Akkadian–English parallel corpus containing 75,562 aligned rows. The release is intended for research in natural language processing, machine translation, and digital humanities. The package includes the primary modeling dataset, derived metadata, an archival copy of the supplied source CSV, validation results, reproducibility scripts, documentation, provenance records, licensing notes, and file checksums. Files File Description AkkadNMT_75K_primary.csv Primary modeling file containing row_id, source_transliteration, and target_translation. AkkadNMT_75K_metadata.csv Derived metadata and validation fields. AkkadNMT_75K_original_eight_column.csv Archival copy of the supplied source CSV. validation_report.json Dataset validation summary. build_release.py Release-building and validation script. data_dictionary.md Field definitions and derivation rules. provenance_manifest.csv Available source and provenance information. license_notes.md Available licensing and redistribution notes. checksums.sha256 SHA-256 checksums for release files. Dataset Summary The final corpus contains 75,562 rows, including 74,420 unique source transliterations and 47,633 unique English translations. No exact duplicate source–translation pairs are present. The source text may contain scholarly transliteration conventions and should not be assumed to follow a single standardized representation. The dataset was assembled from multiple materials. Historical preparation records mention material associated with Old Assyrian Kültepe sources, ORACC, CuneiML, and EvaCun. These reported source quantities are approximate and may overlap. A comparison with the official Deep Past Kaggle archive identified 310 exact aligned-pair matches with its training data. This corpus is not identical to the official competition training dataset. Processing The supplied source CSV was used as the source of truth for the release. The release process performs validation, Unicode NFC normalization, BOM removal where applicable, metadata generation, and integrity checks. The original historical extraction scripts were not retained. Limitations Complete row-level provenance for all records cannot currently be established from the supplied aggregate data. Source versions and licensing details should be verified and completed before publication or redistribution.
